status: PROTOTYPE, UNAUDITED. Nothing is deployed. The owner deploys; never an agent.

notes.contract: stellar/vault (bloch-stellar-vault), built with stellar-cli 30.0.1, soroban-sdk 29.0.1, rustc 1.92.0; source.wasmSha256 is the hash of the round 16 build (docs/STELLAR-BRIDGE-DEPLOY.md section 1) and must be reproduced by the owner before the deploy
notes.config: the object under vault.config is the constructor argument of the contract, verbatim; it is immutable once deployed (no setter, no administrator, no upgrade)
notes.units: amounts are in the L2 token's units: 1 USDC = 1e6 units = 1e7 stroops
notes.token: vault.config.token must equal asset.contract: the Stellar Asset Contract of USDC:GA5ZSEJYB37JRC5AVCIA5MOP4RHTM335X2KGX3IHOJAPP5RE34K4KZVN on the public network. `pairing.py preflight` (before the deploy) and `pairing.py vault-check` (after it) recompute the id from the asset and the network passphrase and refuse anything else; the vault itself accepts any 7-decimal asset contract, so this pin is what stands between a typo and a vault over another asset
notes.labels: source_domain = sha256('stellar-pubnet'), native_domain = sha256('bloch-l2-700770'), asset = sha256('USDC')
notes.limits: the Ethereum bridge's launch values, proposed: cap 100,000 USDC (must equal the L2 supplyCap), window 10,000 USDC per 24 h (must equal the L2 bucketCapacity), minDeposit 11 USDC, l2MinBurn 10 USDC
notes.committee: the same keys as the Ethereum vault: the 7 `eth-release-signer` addresses (5 of 7 release and controls, 6 of 7 unpause) and the 3 `eth-vault-guardian` addresses of docs/BRIDGE-V3-KEY-CEREMONY.md, as 20-byte hex without 0x, each list strictly ascending. No Stellar key holds any power in the vault
notes.releaseDelay: OWNER DECISION, not hard-coded: large_release_threshold and release_delay are constructor values. PROPOSED here (and recommended by rounds 16 and 17): threshold 0 and delay 7,200 s, so every release waits 2 h in the queue, where ONE guardian's pause voids it (guardians can only pause; a pause voids the queue and every older certificate; the committee certifies the real burns again with the ordinary 5 of 7 and they wait the delay again; three hostile guardian keys delay an exit by at most 9 days 8 h with these values). release_delay 0 gives the Ethereum launch behaviour: no queue, the bucket (10,000 USDC a day) is the only bound on a forged release. The delay must be at most half of pause_cooldown (the constructor refuses more). Trade-off and table: docs/STELLAR-BRIDGE.md section 5
notes.fee: 5 bps of each deposit and 5 bps of each release, fixed. fee_recipient is the owner's Stellar address (owner input 2026-11-16). On 2026-11-17 this account does NOT exist on the public network (Horizon 404). The owner runs the fee-account ceremony of docs/STELLAR-BRIDGE-DEPLOY.md section 2 FIRST (create the account with 3 XLM, add the USDC trustline with that account's own key, which proves control of the key); `pairing.py preflight`, `pairing.py vault-check` and `deploy_pontes.py run / verify` all refuse while the account or the trustline is missing
notes.TBD-owner: the 7 signer addresses, the 3 guardian addresses, the deployer account, source.revision, confirmation of the limits, the decision on the release delay, and the fee account ceremony
notes.check: tools/signatario-stellar/pairing.py preflight --vault-config THIS-FILE --config XLM.json before the deploy (policy of this file, Circle's asset, the fee account and its trustline on the network); pairing.py vault-check after it compares every field of vault.config with the deployed vault's config() and refuses any difference. No control is opened and no token is deployed over a vault that fails it

asset.source: Issuer: Circle's list of USDC contract addresses (https://developers.circle.com/stablecoins/usdc-contract-addresses, row Stellar) and the issuer account itself (home domain circle.com, read from Horizon 2026-11-16 and 2026-11-17). Contract: the Stellar Asset Contract id the protocol derives from (network id, USDC, issuer); tools/signatario-stellar/stellar_net.py asset_contract_id recomputes it, and Horizon reports the same id for the asset.
